title: 古朗月行（节选）
author: 李白
intro: What did the moon look like when you were little? Li Bai remembers: a white jade plate, a fairy’s mirror — with an immortal, a cassia tree and a rabbit making medicine up there.
analysis: 诗人回忆小时候看月亮：那时还不认识月亮，就把它叫作“白玉盘”，又怀疑它是仙人瑶台上的镜子，飞到了青云上面。这两个比喻都很像孩子的想法——圆、白、亮、会飞，天真又可爱。后四句写月亮里的传说：月中有仙人，垂着两只脚；有一棵桂树，长得圆圆的、枝叶茂盛；还有一只白兔在捣仙药。诗人好奇地问：药捣好了，要给谁吃呢？这些都是中国古代关于月亮的神话（月宫、桂树、玉兔），今天中秋节时孩子们还会听到。语言简单，想象丰富，很适合初学者朗读。
analysisEn: Li Bai looks back to childhood: before he knew what the moon was, he called it a “white jade plate,” and wondered if it was a mirror from the fairies’ Jade Terrace, flying up above the blue clouds. Both comparisons are exactly how a child thinks — round, white, shiny, and somehow flying — and that is their charm. The next four lines bring in the old stories about the moon. An immortal sits up there with his feet dangling; a cassia tree grows full and round; a white rabbit pounds the medicine of immortality. Then the child’s question: when the medicine is ready, who is going to eat it? These are China’s traditional moon legends — the moon palace, the cassia tree and the Jade Rabbit — still told to children at the Mid-Autumn Festival today. With simple words and a lot of imagination, this is a perfect first poem for reading aloud. The full poem goes on to a darker picture of the moon being eaten away, which is not included here.
background: Li Bai (701–762), the “Immortal of Poetry”, loved the moon more than any other subject. “Old Song of the Bright Moon” is the title of a yuefu (ballad) tune that he rewrote; when and where he wrote it is unknown.
pronunciation: 问言与谁餐：与 yǔ（给）；谁 诗词里传统读 shuí，网站按 shuí 注音。团团 tuán tuán。捣 dǎo。
version: 节选全诗前八句（全诗十六句，后八句写蟾蜍蚀月、后羿射日等）。统编一年级教材只选前四句，网站选前八句。文本与维基文库《全唐诗》本一致；异文：“青云端”一作“白云端”，“何团团”一作“作团团”，“与谁餐”一作“谁与餐”，网站不用。

lines.lit: When I was small I did not know the moon;
lines.en: When I was little and didn’t know the moon,

lines.lit: I called it a white jade plate.
lines.en: I called it a plate of white jade.

lines.lit: I also wondered if it was the mirror of the Jade Terrace,
lines.en: Or maybe, I thought, a mirror from the fairy palace

lines.lit: flying at the tip of the blue clouds.
lines.en: flying high above the blue clouds.

lines.lit: An immortal lets down his two feet;
lines.en: Up there an immortal dangles his feet,

lines.lit: the cassia tree — how round and full!
lines.en: and the cassia tree grows round and thick.

lines.lit: The white rabbit finishes pounding medicine;
lines.en: The white rabbit pounds the magic medicine —

lines.lit: I ask: to whom will it be given to eat?
lines.en: but tell me, who is it for?

words.note: 这里是“小时候”，不是现代汉语的“一个小时”。
“端”是顶上、尽头；“青云”今天还有“平步青云”。
古义“脚”；今天“足球”的“足”还是这个意思。
形容圆而茂密；现代汉语“团团围住”的意思不同。

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 月亮是孩子眼中的白玉盘、仙人的镜子，天真而神奇。
imagery.en: Through a child’s eyes the moon is a jade plate or a fairy’s mirror — innocent and magical.

imagery.name: 桂
imagery.zh: 月中的桂树来自神话，让月亮成了一个有树有人的仙境。
imagery.en: The cassia tree of legend turns the moon into a fairyland with trees and people.

imagery.name: 兔
imagery.zh: 捣药的玉兔是月宫传说里最可爱的角色，引出孩子的好奇提问。
imagery.en: The Jade Rabbit pounding medicine, the sweetest figure in the moon legends, prompts the child’s curious question.
